```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.5,
  dpi = 150

```{r library}
library(quorum)
```

## Why

A colleague has just produced a second fit of the same mixed model, this
time from glmmTMB's Laplace approximation rather than the hub's INLA
backend. Before the two can stand side by side in a quorum, each has to say
what it shares with the other and what it does not -- otherwise "the two
lenses agree" could mean nothing more than "the two lenses share a sampler".
This vignette builds that declaration from the ground up: what a lens must
say about itself, how much two lenses actually share once they say it, and
how far apart their posteriors sit once the sharing is accounted for.

## What

A `quorum_lens()` (built with `lens()`) is a member's fitter behind three
declarations. `shares` names what the lens has in common with every other
lens across four components -- `sampler`, `objective`, `priors` and
`data_prep` -- and is what `quorum_independence()` reads to weigh an
agreement. `expresses` names the response shapes the lens can represent
(`linear`, `plateau`, `threshold`, `nonmonotone`). `scope` is a gate: a
function of the specification that returns `TRUE` inside the lens's corner
and a `quorum_abstention()` outside it, so a model the lens cannot field is
declined rather than mis-fitted. Its `fit(spec, data, ...)` returns a
`quorum_draws()` -- a named list of numeric draws, one vector per parameter,
for a lens of kind `"parameters"` -- or a `quorum_abstention()` when it
cannot answer this particular model. `agreement_pairwise()` compares two
lenses' draws component by component; `quorum()` is the front door that
gates, fits, compares and resolves a whole quorum of lenses at once.

## Do

### Engines available on this build

Two of this vignette's sections need an optional engine each: `lens_tmb()`
needs `glmmTMB` and `tmbstan`, and the hub comparison needs `INLA` through
`flexyBayes::flexybayes()`. Each guarded chunk below checks for its own
engine and prints one sentence in its place when the engine is absent, so the
vignette still renders -- with less to read -- on a build that carries
neither.

```{r engines}
has_tmb <- requireNamespace("glmmTMB", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("tmbstan", quietly = TRUE)
has_inla <- requireNamespace("INLA", quietly = TRUE)
has_ggplot2 <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
engines_ok <- has_tmb && has_inla
```

### A tiny synthetic toy

A synthetic Gaussian random-intercept toy: 60 observations in 6 groups, an
intercept of 2, and a group-level SD of 0.8, seeded for reproducibility. Real
data would work the same way; the toy exists only to keep both fits fast.

```{r toy}
set.seed(20260902)
n <- 60L
n_groups <- 6L
g <- factor(rep(seq_len(n_groups), each = n / n_groups))
u <- rnorm(n_groups, 0, 0.8)
data_toy <- data.frame(y = 2 + u[as.integer(g)] + rnorm(n, 0, 1), g = g)
head(data_toy)
```

### A worked TMB lens

`lens_tmb()` fits glmmTMB's Laplace-approximated marginal likelihood and
then samples the very TMB objective that fit produced with `tmbstan`'s NUTS
sampler -- a second Laplace family distinct from INLA's, and one objective
sampled two ways. The call below keeps the chain count and iteration count
small, which is enough for a toy this size and is exactly what keeps this
vignette fast.

```{r tmb-lens, eval = has_tmb, echo = has_tmb}
tmb_lens <- lens_tmb(chains = 2L, iter = 1000L)
tmb_draws <- tmb_lens@fit(y ~ 1 + (1 | g), data_toy)
tmb_draws@source
names(tmb_draws@draws)
```

```{r tmb-lens-skip, eval = !has_tmb, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat("glmmTMB and/or tmbstan are not installed on this build, so the TMB",
    "lens is not fitted here.\n")
```

### A second lens from the hub

`lens_from_fit()` wraps a model somebody has already fitted -- here, the
hub's own INLA backend on the identical formula -- and canonicalises its
draws onto the same parameter names the TMB lens uses, so the two are
comparable component by component with no relabelling step.

```{r hub-lens, eval = has_inla, echo = has_inla}
withr::local_options(list(flexyBayes.silence_default_prior_note = TRUE))
hub_fit <- flexyBayes::flexybayes(
  y ~ 1 + (1 | g), data = data_toy, backend = "inla", verbose = FALSE,
  seed = 1L
)
hub_lens <- lens_from_fit(hub_fit, name = "inla")
if (is_quorum_abstention(hub_lens)) {
  # a lens that cannot hand over its draws declines, typed, and the rest of
  # the comparison is skipped rather than run against nothing
  print(hub_lens)
  engines_ok <- FALSE
} else {
  hub_draws <- hub_lens@fit(NULL, NULL)
  names(hub_draws@draws)
}
```

```{r hub-lens-skip, eval = !has_inla, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat("INLA is not installed on this build, so the hub comparison lens is",
    "not fitted here.\n")
```

### How much the two lenses actually share

```{r independence, eval = engines_ok, echo = engines_ok}
ind <- quorum_independence(list(tmb_lens, hub_lens))
ind
```

```{r independence-kable, echo = FALSE, eval = engines_ok}
knitr::kable(
  round(ind$weight, 2),
  caption = paste0(
    "Evidential weight between the TMB and INLA lenses (1 = shares ",
    "nothing, 0 = shares everything)."
  )
)
```

```{r independence-skip, eval = !engines_ok, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat("The independence ledger needs both lenses fitted above; it is",
    "skipped when either engine is absent.\n")
```

Both lenses declare every one of the four components differently -- a
Laplace sampler against Stan's NUTS, the TMB objective against INLA's own,
a hub-matched gamma prior against INLA's default fixed-effect prior as the hub applies it, and quorum's
own data preparation against the hub's -- so the ledger gives the pair the
full evidential weight of 1: nothing about their agreement can be explained
by something they share.

### How far apart their posteriors sit

```{r agreement, eval = engines_ok, echo = engines_ok}
agree <- agreement_pairwise(tmb_draws, hub_draws)
agree
```

```{r agreement-kable, echo = FALSE, eval = engines_ok}
knitr::kable(
  agree[, c("param", "mean_a", "mean_b", "sd_ratio", "w1_sd", "verdict")],
  digits = 3,
  caption = paste0(
    "Per-component agreement, TMB lens (a) against the hub's INLA lens (b)."
  )
)
```

```{r agreement-skip, eval = !engines_ok, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat("The agreement table needs both lenses fitted above; it is skipped",
    "when either engine is absent.\n")
```

### Figure: the two posteriors, overlaid

```{r fig-overlay, eval = engines_ok && has_ggplot2, fig.cap = "Posterior density of the intercept under the TMB lens (NUTS over the TMB objective) and the hub's INLA lens, on the same synthetic toy. The subtitle carries the Wasserstein-1 distance between the two, in reference-SD units, from the agreement table above."}
w1_intercept <- agree$w1_sd[agree$param == "(Intercept)"]
overlay_df <- rbind(
  data.frame(value = tmb_draws@draws[["(Intercept)"]], lens = "tmb"),
  data.frame(value = hub_draws@draws[["(Intercept)"]], lens = "inla")
)
ggplot2::ggplot(overlay_df, ggplot2::aes(x = value, fill = lens)) +
  ggplot2::geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "lens") +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "(Intercept)", y = "posterior density",
    title = "Posterior overlay: (Intercept)",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Wasserstein-1 distance = %.2f reference SD", w1_intercept
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```

```{r fig-overlay-skip, eval = !(engines_ok && has_ggplot2), echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat("The posterior overlay needs both lenses fitted and ggplot2",
    "installed; it is skipped when any of the three is absent.\n")
```

### Comparing the two lenses through the front door

```{r quorum-call, eval = engines_ok, echo = engines_ok}
verdict <- quorum(
  list(tmb_lens, hub_lens), spec = y ~ 1 + (1 | g), data = data_toy,
  policy = quorum_policy(order = c("inla", "tmb"), min_lenses = 2L)
)
verdict
```

```{r quorum-call-skip, eval = !engines_ok, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat("The quorum() call needs both lenses fitted above; it is skipped",
    "when either engine is absent.\n")
```

### Writing your own adapter

A lens needs no engine at all -- only a `fit()` that returns a
`quorum_draws()` or a `quorum_abstention()`, and the three declarations
that say what the estimate is worth alongside another lens's. The toy below
moment-matches a Gaussian to the sample mean of `data$y` and declares that it
shares nothing with any engine-backed lens, because it genuinely does not.

```{r custom-lens}
my_fit <- function(spec, data, ...) {
  quorum_draws(
    list(`(Intercept)` = rnorm(200L, mean(data$y), 1)),
    source = "moment_matched"
  )
}
my_lens <- lens(
  name = "toy_moment_match", member = "example", fit = my_fit,
  shares = c(sampler = "none", objective = "moment_matching",
            priors = "none", data_prep = "quorum"),
  expresses = "linear"
)
my_lens@fit(NULL, data_toy)
```

Every built-in lens names its parameter draws on one shared vocabulary, so
that any two lenses -- however different their engines -- line up component
by component with no relabelling: `"(Intercept)"` for the intercept,
the model-matrix column name for every other fixed-effect coefficient,
`"sigma"` for the residual standard deviation, and `"sd_<group>"` for the
standard deviation of a random intercept on grouping variable `<group>`. A
new adapter that wants to sit alongside the built-in lenses names its own
draws on that same vocabulary; a lens that reports a component under any
other name simply will not be found by `agreement_pairwise()` when it looks
for what the two lenses have in common.

## Read

```{r read-prep, echo = FALSE}
read_w1 <- if (engines_ok) round(w1_intercept, 2L) else NA_real_
read_verdict <- if (engines_ok) verdict@status else NA_character_
read_carried <- if (engines_ok) {
  verdict@resolution$carried_lens[1L]
} else {
  NA_character_
}
```

```{r read-text, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
if (engines_ok) {
  cat(
    "On this run the intercept sits", read_w1,
    "reference SDs apart under the Wasserstein-1 distance, and the",
    "pair's overall verdict is", paste0("`", read_verdict, "`."),
    "The front door carries the", paste0("`", read_carried, "`"),
    "lens's answer regardless -- `quorum()` compares lenses, it never",
    "prices a decision, so with no `decide` argument the carried answer",
    "is `NA` and only the comparison itself is reported. Two lenses that",
    "share nothing can still disagree: independence is what makes an",
    "agreement worth something, not a guarantee that one will be found.",
    "The random-intercept SD (`sd_g`) is the harder component here, which",
    "is expected on a toy this small -- six groups leave little",
    "information for a variance component, and the Laplace",
    "approximation underlying the TMB lens is at its least reliable",
    "exactly there.\n"
  )
} else {
  cat(
    "glmmTMB, tmbstan or INLA is not installed on this build, so the",
    "comparison above did not run; the sections marked skipped state",
    "which engine was missing.\n"
  )
}
```

## Limits

This toy is synthetic and deliberately small, chosen to keep both samplers
fast rather than to stress either engine: six groups is too few to identify
a random-intercept SD precisely under any method, which is part of why that
component agrees less well than the intercept above. The independence
ledger reads only what a lens declares about itself; it cannot discover an
undeclared dependency, so a lens that mis-states its own `shares` will mislead
the ledger in a way no computation here can catch. Agreement between two
lenses fitted to the same data, as both are here, is agreement about that
dataset, not independent corroboration of the fact behind it -- the caveat
`quorum_independence()` attaches to every such pair says so explicitly, and
it is not repeated numerically in this vignette's figure or tables.

## What to read next

*A quorum of lenses on Study A0* applies the front door to 200 recorded
decision cells and generalises the two-lens cascade this vignette's `quorum()`
call is a miniature of. *Getting started with quorum* introduces the three
on-ramps -- ensemble ingestion, surrogate emulation, and the koine fourth
opinion -- that turn a non-hub estimate into a lens without writing an
adapter like the one built here.

## Reproduce

Seed `20260902` for the synthetic toy; `seed = 1L` inside `lens_tmb()`'s
default and passed explicitly to `flexyBayes::flexybayes()`. Package
versions follow.

```{r session-info}
sessionInfo()
```
